Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Theme: Course Orientation / Fundamentals of Thermodynamics / Types of Energy and Physical Constants
Details: This lecture explains the overall purpose of the course, demonstrating why thermodynamics is crucial for considering energy production. It organizes fundamental concepts such as energy, work, and heat, providing a scientific understanding of representative energy forms, including kinetic energy, potential energy, chemical energy, electrical energy, and thermal energy. It confirms the meaning of units and physical constants frequently used in thermodynamics, solidifying the foundation for understanding future lectures.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: We examine the First Law of Thermodynamics, known as the law of energy conservation, and learn about the relationship between internal energy, heat, and work. Through the process of energy changing form, moving, and transforming, we understand the concept of energy balance. Using concrete examples such as power generation and chemical reactions, we consider why, despite energy never being lost, there are constraints on how it can be utilized.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: This section addresses the Second Law of Thermodynamics, which governs the irreversibility of natural phenomena. It introduces the concept of entropy and provides a scientific explanation for why energy conversion inevitably involves loss and why not all energy can be effectively utilized. Using the upper limit of thermal engine efficiency as an example, it helps understand that fundamental limitations exist in energy utilization.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: Introduce the concept of free energy and learn which portion of energy can be extracted as work. Focusing on Gibbs free energy, understand the relationship with reactions that proceed spontaneously and with equilibrium states. Through these concepts, be able to thermodynamically explain why chemical reactions and battery reactions proceed.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: We examine exergy as an indicator that evaluates not only the “quantity” but also the “quality” of energy. By considering the First and Second Laws of Thermodynamics, we learn to compare electrical energy with high-temperature heat and low-temperature heat, and to evaluate energy from the perspective of usability. This enables a scientific understanding of why waste heat and untapped energy resources arise.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: Batteries are examined as representative energy conversion and storage devices, explaining the relationship between chemical energy and electrical energy from a thermodynamic perspective. Students will understand the relationship between a battery's electromotive force and free energy change, learning the physical significance of metrics such as energy density and efficiency. Through examples like lithium-ion batteries and fuel cells, the fundamentals of energy conversion technology will be understood.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: Using the thermodynamic concepts learned thus far, examine energy issues in renewable energy and a decarbonized society. Considering the thermodynamic constraints associated with energy conversion and storage, develop the perspective to scientifically evaluate entire energy systems while distinguishing between what is technically feasible and what presents difficulties.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: We will review the fundamental concepts of thermodynamics covered throughout the course and their applications, reaffirming the perspective for scientifically explaining energy generation. Subsequently, a final exam will be administered to assess conceptual understanding and logical explanatory skills.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Theme: What is Policy Sociology: Sociology and Public Policy
Details: Burawoy's four types, positioning of policy sociology, relationship between sociology and public policy. Work: Identify familiar policies and consider who designed them with what assumptions.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: Understanding Public Policy: Policy Process and Actors
Details: Policy cycle (problem definition → agenda setting → formation → decision → implementation → evaluation), foundations of policy process theory, actor mapping. Work: Map policy actors for child/childcare support.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: State, Governance, and Institutions: Who Decides Policy
Details: Political sociology and state theory, welfare state theory (Esping-Andersen, etc.), governance theory. Work: Compare "state-centered model" and "governance network model" in healthcare/elderly care.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: Evidence, Expert Knowledge and Policy: Sociology of EBPM
Details: EBPM ideals and reality, role and limitations of social surveys/statistics, epistemic communities. Work: Examine "what is measured and what is invisible" in white papers/statistics.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: Inequality and Social Policy: Class, Gender, and Minorities
Details: Class/poverty/precarity and social policy, gender order and family policy, minority policy and inclusion/exclusion. Work: Extract family models/labor views underlying welfare/parental leave policies.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: Risk, Environment, and Globalization: Policy from Contemporary Social Theory
Details: Risk society theory/environmental sociology, globalization and policy (international organizations/multinationals/citizen movements), Japanese issues (aging/regional revitalization). Work: Critical examination of SDGs targets and Japanese policies.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: Possibilities and Limitations of Policy Sociology: Summary and Group Presentations
Details: Review of key concepts, self-reflection on policy sociology (dilemma between client orientation and criticality). Group presentations: Each group analyzes one policy topic sociologically (approx. 10 min).

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Details: Aims and procedures of policy sociology research. Introduction to typical research themes. Group formation and theme selection. Homework: Find 2 policy documents and 1 academic paper.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Theme: Finding Literature/Resources and Prior Research Review
Details: Types and roles of literature (academic papers, policy documents, statistical data). Basics of literature review. Group literature introduction and organization. Homework: Create 2-3 page literature review.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Theme: Creating Analytical Framework: How to Use Theory
Details: Introduction to representative analytical axes (inequality, governance, risk, evidence). Create concept maps in groups. How to apply theory to own cases. Homework: Write 1-2 page analytical framework.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Theme: Reading Policy Documents and Data: Case Study Design
Details: How to read policy documents (problem definition, goals, institutional design, etc.). How to select cases (time series, regional comparison, etc.). Group policy document analysis. Interim report. Homework: Create 3-4 page interim report.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Details: Policy evaluation perspectives (distributional impact, normative aspects, implementation gaps). Discussion of current policy issues and improvement directions. Alternative proposal conception. Homework: Create draft slides/handouts for final presentation.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Theme: Final Presentation Preparation and Peer Review
Details: Presentation structure (problem setting → prior research → framework → analysis → implications). Practice presentations by groups. Feedback using peer review sheets. Homework: Complete final presentation materials.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Details: Each group presents 10-12 min + 5 min Q&A. Instructor comments (theoretical contributions, future development potential). Overall discussion: Strengths and limitations of policy sociological approaches. Submit individual final report.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Details: The overall objectives, goals, schedule, and evaluation methods of the course will be explained. | Students will introduce themselves and share their academic backgrounds and areas of concern. | As the starting point of the course, students will attempt to relive and analyze the experience of "becoming a disaster victim" based on concrete case studies from past major disasters.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Theme: Systems and Philosophies of Relief and Livelihood Recovery
Details: Students will learn about the processes and related systems from immediate post-disaster relief to long-term livelihood recovery, as well as the underlying philosophies that shape them.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Theme: Urban Disasters and Reconstruction Case Studies
Details: This session focuses on case studies of urban disaster recovery, including reconstruction projects, urban planning, and community redevelopment processes following the Great Kanto Earthquake and the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Theme: Recovery in Mountainous and Coastal Areas
Details: Students will study recovery processes in rural and coastal areas, including examples from the 2004 Niigata Chuetsu Earthquake, the 2007 Noto Peninsula Earthquake, and the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake. Topics include reconstruction projects, collective relocation, village restoration, and industrial recovery.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Details: Based on case studies of the Great East Japan Earthquake and the 2019 Typhoon #19, students will explore how disaster information and community response influence evacuation in the face of floods and tsunamis.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Details: Students will examine the role of volunteers in disaster recovery and risk reduction, how their roles differ from those of the public sector, and how related systems have evolved over time. | The concept of “support” itself will also be discussed, drawing insights from research in the field of care.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Theme: Psychological Care and Disaster Memory Transmission
Details: This session introduces the basic concepts, institutional developments, and challenges of medicalization in psychological trauma care caused by disaster experiences. | Students will also study the transmission of disaster memory as part of the recovery process for victims and affected communities, focusing on case studies from the Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake and the Great East Japan Earthquake.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Details: The course concludes with a written exam consisting of true/false questions to assess factual understanding and essay questions that address fundamental issues in disaster prevention and recovery.
